title: Effects of interviewers on response to income and wealth items
summary: This paper examines whether interviewer expectations about respondents' willingness to report income are associated with actual item responses to income and asset questions in Wave 6 of the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE). Using data from 41,934 respondents across 12 countries, the study analyzes responses to four financial items with substantial nonresponse and compares three approaches for handling missing covariates.
key_points: Study analyzes 41,934 respondents in 12 countries from SHARE Wave 6
Examines four financial items with substantial item nonresponse
Respondents interviewed by interviewers with higher expected income response rates are more likely to provide financial information
Three methods compared for handling missing covariates: complete-case analysis, multiple imputation, and generalized missing-indicator framework with model averaging
Model averaging does not yield clear gains over simpler approaches
Findings have implications for interviewer training and survey fieldwork design
why_it_matters: This research is relevant to survey methodology and data quality in economic research. Understanding interviewer effects on survey nonresponse could improve the reliability of wealth and income data collected in major surveys, which may indirectly inform economic research. However, this paper does not address market structure or macro catalysts directly.
